title: Two bankruptcies in the numbers that survive
lede: Lionel was a public company, but its filings predate EDGAR and are not online. Every figure we could confirm from court opinions and the press of the time is here. The gaps in the charts are gaps in the record, not zeros.

blocks.title: Stores: built, halved, rebuilt, liquidated
blocks.subtitle: Lionel’s toy stores under all names, at the dates a source gives a count.
blocks.xLabel: Date of the report (not evenly spaced)

points.title: the first peak
points.text: 105 stores, after buying 26 in Texas and the Midwest in 1980. Chapter 11 follows on February 19, 1982.[^1][^2][^4]

points.title: cut by half
points.text: 56 stores a year into the first bankruptcy.[^4]

points.title: the comeback
points.text: 90 stores in 16 states and a new store in Manhattan.[^10]

points.title: the second filing
points.text: 97 stores on June 14, 1991. The company had 101 before it began closing them.[^16][^20]

points.title: the retreat
points.text: 29 stores in six markets after the Christmas of 1992.[^23]

points.title: the vote
points.text: 28 stores when the creditors’ committee votes to liquidate.[^24][^27]

blocks.source: Counts as reported: 105 and 56[^4], 59[^8], 90[^10], 97[^16][^17], 71[^20], 69[^22], 29[^23], 28[^24][^25]. A 1982 Times article gives “more than 90 stores in 22 states” for the same period as the 105 figure[^1]; a 2017 retrospective gives “more than 150”, which no contemporary source we found supports.[^28]

blocks.title: Sales, in the years a figure survives
blocks.subtitle: Lionel Corporation revenue, $ millions. Only six years are documented in our sources.
blocks.source: 1981 and 1982: Second Circuit opinion[^2]. 1987[^10]. Fiscal years ended January 1990 and January 31, 1991[^16]. Fiscal year ended January 30, 1993[^26][^27]. The 1981–82 figures are consolidated and include Dale Electronics. Years not shown are not in our sources.

blocks.title: Profit and loss, where reported
blocks.subtitle: $ millions. Four results over eleven years, and the basis differs between them.
blocks.source: 1982: “some $51 million” lost[^4]. 1987: earned $5.8M[^10]. Year to January 1990: an operating profit of $300,000, not a net figure; year to January 31, 1991: a loss of $5.9M[^16]. Year to January 30, 1993: a loss of $100.3M[^26][^27]. The 1982 bankruptcy petition separately gave a $5.5M loss for 1981.[^1]

blocks.title: Where the 101 stores of 1991 went
blocks.subtitle: Store closings between the second bankruptcy and the liquidation vote.

to.label: Still open at the liquidation vote

blocks.source: 101 stores and 30 closings in 1991[^20]; 28 stores at liquidation[^24][^25]. The middle figure is derived. Sources differ by a store or two from month to month, and at least one store opened in this period, so treat the split as approximate.

rows.text: working-capital line the banks declined to renew in 1991[^16]
